summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and alcohol abuse, was admitted with chest pain and hemoptysis. A CT scan revealed an acute pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe with associated pulmonary infarct and pleural effusion. He was started on anticoagulation with Lovenox and prescribed Coumadin for long-term management, with Pradaxa and aspirin discontinued. Despite clear explanation of the life-threatening risks, he chose to leave against medical advice. At discharge, he was alert, oriented, and demonstrated understanding of his treatment plan, including medication instructions and the need for INR monitoring. He was sent home with prescriptions and strict instructions to avoid alcohol and seek immediate care for worsening symptoms.
